understanding the role of feedback from active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the evolution of early‐type galaxies, and in particular the role of AGN feedback in driving the migration of galaxies from the blue cloud into the red sequence.

the observed evolution of early type galaxies is consistent with a scenario in which the AGN is the dominant mechanism for gas removal.

The main takeaway from our work is that
AGN feedback is required to explain the rapid migration of star-forming early types from the blue cloud onto the red sequence.
the migration of blue early-types to the red sequence is a rapid process that is likely to be driven by the AGN.
